headline: Your Uxopian waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing document-heavy buyers into the right Content API switch, legacy-ECM modernization, content-ops hiring, or soft modernization offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Corto Romagny.
productSummary: Uxopian Software (uxopian.com) is a European-origin enterprise content + document-AI platform (OEM and enterprise). Product suite: FlowerDocs (NoSQL content repository, multi-tenant, process orchestration / eProcess); ARender (universal IDP viewer — 250–500+ formats, annotation, redaction, white-label); Fast2 (visual ECM migration + enrichment with 15+ connectors); Uxopian AI (classification, extraction, summarization, Ask Repository, Zero-Scroll Summaries, Contract Compare, Xopia Bot, Smart Tagging, Process Intelligence); Content API Platform (REST + Web Components for SaaS/BPO teams to embed storage, viewing, migration, and AI under their own brand). Homepage framing: Modernize Legacy ECMs with AI powered Document Processing. Solution pillars: Content Infrastructure, Compliance & Automation, Modernization & UX, SaaS & BPO Acceleration. Deployment: on-prem, private cloud, or SaaS — sovereignty as a feature for banking, insurance, financial services, and public sector. Public proof on homepage / partner pages: 50B+ documents migrated; 1T+ metadata updates executed; 35+ successful projects delivered; 50+ TCS engineers certified on Uxopian; partner since 2019 with continued annual growth 25%+. Named proof: CGI Trade360 — Philip Cutrone (Trade360 Solution Architect) — API-first multi-tenant document foundation accelerated CGI Trade360 in 9 months. Content API page marketing claims (flag as vendor claims, not third-party audited): DIY document storage/viewer often costs $200K–$500K and 6–12 months; staging integration in under 5 days; Fast2 example of 2.4M docs migrated in ~4.2h with 0.02% error rate (demo/marketing figures on content-api-platform page). Corto Romagny is GM, Uxopian International Corp (US / North America expansion) per uxopian.com/en/about-us; Allison (allison@usegtmx.co) offered a 5-page cold-email strategy doc and Corto replied Yes please.
coreInsight: Corto sells one content layer — FlowerDocs + ARender + Fast2 + Uxopian AI — not a different product per vertical. Banking vs insurance vs SaaS/BPO is a merge tag after routing, not a second waterfall. The single routing signal is content_stack_state from BuiltWith + LinkedIn Jobs + careers/site scrape: competing document viewer/SDK, legacy ECM platform, content/ECM hiring with no stack match, or none of those. That ladder maps to Uxopian’s live offers (white-label Content API consolidation, legacy modernization without rip-and-replace + Fast2, AI-on-existing-repos for content ops teams, soft Content Modernization Playbook for remaining TAM) and keeps one durable list for North America outbound.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is which content stack they already run
sections.takeaway: BuiltWith + LinkedIn Jobs + a careers/site scrape already names a competing document viewer/SDK, a legacy ECM (Documentum, FileNet, Alfresco, SharePoint Server…), content/ECM hiring with no stack match, or none of those. That content_stack_state is stronger than a title guess and cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every in-TAM document buyer
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Competing viewer/SDK first, then legacy ECM detected, then content/ECM hiring with no Tier 1–2 stack, then every remaining in-TAM regulated or document-heavy buyer.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each content-stack state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Viewer/SDK shops get a Content API Switch Brief. Legacy ECM shops get a Modernize-Without-Rip Brief. Content-ops hiring gets an AI-on-Your-Repos Brief. The rest get the soft Content Modernization Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the viewer, modernize the ECM, brief the content hire, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always document-heavy buyers Uxopian already sells into (banking, insurance, FS, public sector, SaaS/BPO, SIs). Vertical is a merge tag. A/Bs sit on exclusive routes (sovereignty vs speed-to-ship).

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the stack already on their site or Jobs page
sections.takeaway: Notice the viewer, the legacy ECM, or the content hire, poke the glue-layer / rip-and-replace / capacity pain that state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the competing-viewer route first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already pay Apryse, Nutrient, Foxit, or a peer and still stitch storage + AI + migration. Prove reply density, then roll legacy-ECM modernization, content-ops hiring, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Apollo + LinkedIn Sales Nav filtered to Uxopian’s commercial TAM (banking, insurance, financial services, public sector, document-heavy SaaS/BPO, systems integrators) and mid-market-to-enterprise headcount is the spine Corto already sells into in North America. Public TAM account count is not published on uxopian.com; treat size as estimated (see uxopian-magnet-flags.txt) and keep each launch tier ≥~1,500 contacts where possible.

BuiltWith + LinkedIn Jobs + careers/site scrape returns content_stack_state in one pull: competing document viewer/SDK (Apryse/PDFTron, Nutrient/PSPDFKit, Foxit, Adobe Embed/PDF API, Aspose, Box View) for Tier 1; legacy ECM (OpenText Documentum, IBM FileNet, Alfresco, Nuxeo, OpenText Content Server, SharePoint Server) for Tier 2; content/ECM hiring titles with no Tier 1–2 stack for Tier 3 — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Uxopian offers on uxopian.com: white-label Content API / OEM consolidation for viewer-SDK shops; FlowerDocs + ARender overlay + Fast2 migration for legacy ECM; Uxopian AI on existing repositories for content-ops hiring; soft Content Modernization Playbook for remaining TAM — plus CGI Trade360 (9 months) and 50B+ docs migrated as proof.

Buyer title (CTO / VP Eng / Head of Digital / Head of Content / ECM Architect / COO) and vertical (insurance, banking, FS, public sector, SaaS/BPO) are scrape filters and merge tags, not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the account is routed.

sources.name: BuiltWith + company tech / integration pages
sources.delivers: content_stack_state for competing document viewers/SDKs (Tier 1) and legacy ECM platforms (Tier 2). Primary routing signal when the stack is publicly detectable.

sources.name: LinkedIn Jobs + company careers pages
sources.delivers: Confirms Tier 1–2 stack via job text (Documentum, FileNet, Apryse, PDFTron…) and delivers Tier 3 content/ECM hiring titles when no stack match. Same pull as soft prioritisation inside a tier.

sources.name: Apollo + LinkedIn Sales Nav (vertical + headcount filters)
sources.delivers: In-TAM accounts across banking, insurance, FS, public sector, document-heavy SaaS/BPO, and SIs plus buyer titles. The TAM spine.

sources.name: Company site / product / docs pages (optional personalisation)
sources.delivers: stack_hint and document-workflow language for copy merge tags after routing. Do not use absence-of-tool alone as a Tier 1–2 trigger unless the tool would be visibly proven if present (careers/site mentions count).

sources.name: Apollo email enrichment (after qualification)
sources.delivers: Work emails for already-routed accounts. Do not buy a raw ‘CTO list’ and hope.

sources.name: Optional Uxopian customer / partner suppress
sources.delivers: Current-customer and active-partner exclusion when Corto shares an account list (CGI, TCS footprint is proof, not a complete exclude list). Treat as suppress, not a tier.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_viewer_detected = true (BuiltWith / careers / site names Apryse, PDFTron, Nutrient, PSPDFKit, Foxit, Adobe Embed/PDF Services, Aspose, Box View, or equivalent document viewer/SDK) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They already buy document viewing/SDK capacity and still stitch storage, migration, and AI across vendors. Strongest intent for Uxopian’s white-label Content API Platform (FlowerDocs + ARender + Fast2 + AI under one OEM contract). Proof path: CGI Trade360 in 9 months; Content API page claims weeks-to-ship vs DIY $200K–$500K / 6–12 months.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND legacy_ecm_detected = true (Documentum, IBM FileNet, Alfresco, Nuxeo, OpenText Content Server, SharePoint Server / on-prem SharePoint as ECM) AND no Tier-1 competing viewer/SDK AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They run a legacy repository the business still depends on — pain is AI, governance, and multi-format viewing without a rip-and-replace programme. Maps to ARender overlay + Uxopian AI on existing repos + Fast2 when data must move. Homepage: Modernize Legacy ECMs; blog: modernize without replatforming; 50B+ docs migrated.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND content_hiring_open = true (ECM admin, Documentum/FileNet/Alfresco specialist, records manager, content platform / document engineer, IDP / document-AI engineer) AND no Tier 1–2 stack match AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They are buying content capacity via hiring — soft high-intent before catch-all. Maps to Uxopian AI on existing repositories (Zero-Scroll Summaries, extraction, Ask Repository) plus optional FlowerDocs/ARender without forcing a platform swap on Day 0.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (document-heavy regulated or SaaS/BPO buyers). Soft CTA around governed content, sovereignty, and a free first conversation. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Competing document viewer / SDK detected
tiers.trigger: BuiltWith, careers, or site names Apryse/PDFTron, Nutrient/PSPDFKit, Foxit, Adobe Embed/PDF Services, Aspose, Box View, or equivalent; not already a Uxopian customer
tiers.pain: They already pay for a viewer/SDK and still act as the glue between storage, migration, and AI vendors — every sprint on document infrastructure is a sprint not spent on product.
tiers.valueProp: Content API Switch Brief: white-label FlowerDocs + ARender + Fast2 + Uxopian AI under one OEM / per-tenant license, deploy on-prem or their cloud. Anchored to CGI Trade360 (9 months) and Content API page claims (weeks vs DIY $200K–$500K / 6–12 months).
tiers.dataSource: BuiltWith + careers/site scrape for competing viewer/SDK names
tiers.replyDensity: Highest - they already buy document infrastructure
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; not published on uxopian.com — keep each tier ≥~1,500 contacts before launch when the niche allows

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Legacy ECM detected, no competing viewer/SDK
tiers.trigger: In-TAM company shows Documentum, IBM FileNet, Alfresco, Nuxeo, OpenText Content Server, or SharePoint Server as ECM with no Tier-1 viewer/SDK match
tiers.pain: The repository still runs the business, but AI, multi-format viewing, and governance sit behind a multi-year rip-and-replace fear — support clocks and AI expectations land at the same time.
tiers.valueProp: Modernize-Without-Rip Brief: ARender + Uxopian AI on content where it already lives; Fast2 when migration is required (15+ connectors, homepage 50B+ docs migrated). No forced replatform on Day 0.
tiers.dataSource: BuiltWith + careers/site for legacy ECM names after viewer/SDK filter fails
tiers.replyDensity: High - visible platform constraint, clear modernization path

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Content / ECM hiring only
tiers.trigger: In-TAM company posts ECM admin, Documentum/FileNet/Alfresco specialist, records manager, content platform / document engineer, or document-AI / IDP roles with no Tier 1–2 stack match
tiers.pain: Open content roles mean months of recruiting while classification, extraction, and case screens stay manual — peers already ship AI summaries into claims, loans, and HR.
tiers.valueProp: AI-on-Your-Repos Brief: Uxopian AI (Zero-Scroll Summaries, extraction, Ask Repository) on existing repositories; optional FlowerDocs/ARender when ready — European-origin, on-prem capable.
tiers.dataSource: LinkedIn Jobs + careers for content/ECM titles after Tier 1–2 filters fail
tiers.replyDensity: Medium - clear buying window, longer education cycle

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM document-heavy buyers
tiers.trigger: In-TAM company in banking, insurance, FS, public sector, document-heavy SaaS/BPO, or SI with a CTO / VP Eng / Head of Digital / Head of Content decision maker and no Tier 1–3 content_stack_state
tiers.pain: Day-to-day ops still run on fragmented repositories and manual document handling, so AI and governed content stay on the ‘someday’ list while regulated peers modernize.
tiers.valueProp: Soft Content Modernization Playbook: how peers in {{vertical}} start with a viewer overlay or narrow AI use case, then Content API / FlowerDocs — 50B+ docs migrated, CGI Trade360 in 9 months, soft CTA.
tiers.dataSource: Apollo / Sales Nav after in_tam gate
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; catch-all must cover remaining TAM
